overview: Baekje was renowned for its refined Buddhist culture, maritime trade networks and artistic achievements. It played a crucial role in transmitting Chinese learning and Buddhism to Japan, shaping East Asian cultural development.

items.text: Maritime trade connected Korea to China, Japan and possibly Southeast Asia.
Baekje sent Buddhist texts, images and monks to Japan, officially introducing Buddhism.
The Baekje smile on Buddhist sculptures represents a distinctive aesthetic achievement.
Gold-bronze Buddhist statues and reliquaries show sophisticated craftsmanship.
The Gilt-bronze Incense Burner exemplifies Baekje metalworking artistry.
Buddhism officially adopted as state religion, leading to temple construction and monastic communities.
Confucian learning and Chinese classics studied by the aristocratic elite.
Baekje Historic Areas designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Its cultural transmission to Japan profoundly influenced Japanese civilization.

fall.text: Silla forces allied with Tang China conquered Baekje in 660, capturing the capital Sabi and ending the kingdom.
